findings.summary: The refactor dropped `failed=$((failed + 1))` from the wildcard/failure branch of the migrate `case` statement (it was present pre-refactor). Individual migrate failures (auth errors, 5xx, malformed payload, etc.) are now printed to stderr but no longer counted in `failed`, so the closing `[[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]] || exit 1` (line 171) will exit 0 even when repos failed to mirror. This silently breaks the nightly cron job's success/failure signal — exactly the kind of per-repo failure the brief asked to be reliably branched on via status codes.

findings.summary: gh_api (used for every GitHub call, including the paginated `/user/repos` enumeration `while` loop) has no `--max-time`, unlike gitea_api which got `--max-time 60`/`1800`. The brief explicitly says 'bound how long any single request can run' — as implemented that only applies to Gitea calls; a stalled connection to api.github.com can still hang the script indefinitely.
